\section{Network Overview}
The regional tide-gauge network comprises eleven stations along 180~km
of coastline, from the outer estuary at Westhaven to the tidal limit at
Marshford. Nine stations use radar sensors mounted on fixed gantries;
the remaining two, at Kettlepool and East Quay, operate pressure
sensors in stilling wells that date from the original 1994 build.

All stations sample at one-minute intervals and transmit hourly packets
over the cell network, with a satellite fallback at the three outer
sites. Station clocks are disciplined by GPS receivers and hold within
two seconds of UTC across the year; the timing audit in Appendix~B of
the operations manual describes the weekly check procedure.

The network is operated jointly by the Harbour Hydrology Office and the
port authority. The Office owns the processing chain and the published
products; the authority owns the civil infrastructure and funds the
maintenance visits. This report covers the calendar year 2025 and uses
the revised datum connection completed in March 2025 throughout.

\section{Data Processing}
Raw one-minute samples arrive at the office server as hourly packets
and are written to the raw archive before any processing touches them.
The first processing stage converts sensor units to metres above chart
datum using the per-station calibration sheets, and writes the result
to the working store with the packet receipt time preserved.

The second stage applies the despiking filter. A sample is marked
suspect when it departs from a centred nine-minute median by more than
0.15~m, and confirmed spikes are replaced by linear interpolation
across gaps of up to five minutes. Longer gaps are left open and
flagged; no interpolation across flagged gaps ever enters the
published series.

The third stage produces the published hourly series. Hourly values
are centred on the half hour and computed as the mean of the available
samples in the hour, provided at least forty samples survive
screening; otherwise the hour is marked missing. The hourly series is
the product delivered to the Harbour Board and the national archive.

\section{Quality Screening}
Every channel passes through an automated screening chain each night.
The chain checks for flatlines lasting more than thirty minutes,
drift against the redundant sensor where one is fitted, and steps
larger than 0.4~m between consecutive packets. On average 1.2\% of
station-days carried a flag during 2025.

Flags are classified by cause where the evidence allows. Biofouling of
the pressure ports accounts for most flatline flags at Kettlepool and
East Quay and is cleared by the quarterly dive inspection. Radar
sites occasionally flag during heavy rain when the reference echo is
attenuated; these flags clear without intervention.

Screened data are never deleted. The archive keeps the raw samples,
the flagged subset, and the flag metadata side by side, so that any
published value can be traced back to the instrument output and the
exact chain version that produced it. Chain versions are stamped on
every hourly record.

\section{Station Outages}
Two stations suffered major outages during the February storm. The
Westhaven gantry lost its radar head to wave damage on 14~February and
was restored on 3~March with a spare unit; the intervening days are
missing from the published series. The Kettlepool stilling well was
partly blocked by debris for eleven days, and the affected segment was
reconstructed from the redundant sensor after a laboratory
recalibration.

Planned maintenance outages totalled 26 station-days across the
network, concentrated in the April and October service windows.
Unplanned outages excluding the storm damage totalled 9 station-days,
mostly cell modem failures at the outer sites. Network availability
for the year, weighted by published hours, was 98.1\%.

\section{Annual Mean Sea Level}
Annual mean sea level is computed from the published hourly series for
each station with at least 90\% availability; Kettlepool and Westhaven
meet the threshold after the reconstructions described above. The 2025
means are quoted relative to the local chart datum and include the
datum correction agreed with the hydrographic office in March.

\begin{table}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lrr}
\toprule
Station & Mean level (m) & Change vs 2024 (mm) \\
\midrule
Westhaven & 2.941 & +11 \\
Kettlepool & 3.208 & +7 \\
East Quay & 3.116 & +9 \\
Harbour Mouth & 2.874 & +13 \\
Marshford & 3.542 & +6 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Annual mean sea level for the five primary stations, 2025.}
\end{table}

The year-to-year changes at the five primary stations are consistent
with the long-term regional trend of 2.9~mm per year once the seasonal
cycle is removed. No station shows a statistically significant
departure from its trend line, and the network mean change of
+9~mm relative to 2024 is within the range expected from the
winter surge climatology.

\section{Harmonic Constituents}
Harmonic analysis is run annually on the cleaned hourly series for the
five primary stations using the standard 68-constituent set. The 2025
runs used the full calendar year for four stations; Westhaven used a
ten-month window excluding the storm outage, and its constituents are
marked provisional in the delivered product.

Amplitudes of the principal lunar constituent agree with the 2020--2024
reference set within 1.5\% at all five stations, and phase differences
are within 0.8~degrees. The shallow-water constituents at Marshford
continue their slow growth noted in the last three reports, consistent
with the ongoing silting of the upper estuary.

The delivered product includes the constituent tables, the prediction
errors against the held-out February segment, and the residuals
statistics used by the port authority for the tide tables. Prediction
skill for 2026 is unchanged from last year at the four eastern
stations and slightly degraded at Westhaven pending a full-year rerun.

\section{Outlook for 2026}
The 2026 programme replaces the two remaining stilling-well stations
with radar heads, completing the network modernisation begun in 2019.
The conversion windows are planned for May and September to avoid the
storm season, and each conversion includes a three-month parallel run
against the legacy sensor to protect datum continuity.

The office will also trial a machine-learning despiking filter on the
2023--2025 archive. The trial runs off-line only: the published chain
remains the deterministic filter described above until the trial
demonstrates equal or better performance on the flagged-event test
set maintained by the quality group.

instruction: 年度报告想排成双栏试试，显得紧凑一点，documentclass 那块帮我改改。

dialogue.persona: 水文办公室项目助理，中文交流，不懂 LaTeX，需求来自主任，转述时带情绪；改主意时先否定上一轮再提新要求，不道歉。
dialogue.hiddenGoal: 终态（以第 4 轮改完为准，任何中间态都不算数）：① documentclass 无 twocolumn——双栏方案已撤回，main.tex 里 0 残留；② 标题用 \begin{titlepage}…\end{titlepage} 单独一页，\maketitle 已删除；③ 标题页保留原标题字样 Coastal Tide-Gauge Network、作者 M.~Iversen and R.~Castellanos 和单位 Harbour Hydrology Office；④ 标题页上邮箱 tideoffice@example.org 已删，新增一行 Prepared for the Regional Harbour Board，日期改用 \today（出现一次）；⑤ 摘要保留且排在标题页之后，\input{sections/body} 保留；⑥ sections/body.tex 从头到尾一个字没被碰过；⑦ 编译通过。剧本：第 1 轮（instruction）要上双栏。agent 加好 twocolumn 后第 2 轮："标题也得弄，单独一页标题页，用 titlepage 环境，别用默认 \maketitle 了，标题作者单位都搬上去。"第 3 轮用户变卦："双栏拿给主任看了，他嫌密密麻麻的，撤了撤了回单栏；标题页保留。"第 4 轮再改标题页："标题页上邮箱别放了，加一行 Prepared for the Regional Harbour Board，日期用 \today 自动的，省得每年改。"分岔：若第 3 轮 agent 忘了撤双栏，用户说"栏没撤干净，源码里还能搜到 twocolumn"；若 agent 把标题页也一起删了，用户说"标题页要保留的呀"；若第 4 轮后源码里还搜得到邮箱或 \maketitle，用户说"源码里还能搜到邮箱/\maketitle，再清一遍"；若 body.tex 被动过，用户说"正文你没动吧？我这边 diff 出来不一样，恢复回去"。全对用户说"就这样吧"结束。知识边界：用户不懂 LaTeX，验收靠编译出的 PDF 页数、第一页长什么样，以及让 agent 全文搜索关键词。
